status: PASS bounded CPU/CUDA F32 PowerOfTwo dynamic linear
problem: The public Float8BlockLinear contract admitted F32 A with PowerOfTwo dynamic group128 quantization, but the CUDA route declined it because its embedded pow2 Triton quantizer only accepted BF16.

implementation.new_path: Existing native F32 PowerOfTwo quantizer writes E4 codes and row-major F32[M,K/128] scales into the existing caller-owned encoded activation workspace, then the existing F32-output encoded GEMM runs on the original shared CUDA queue.
implementation.unchanged_path: The original BF16 pow2 Triton entry remains explicitly BF16-only and retains column-major activation scales. Divide and MultiplyReciprocal routes and their original modules remain unchanged.
implementation.layout: The GEMM launch chooses scale strides from the actual selected quantizer carrier. New native F32 uses row-major group strides; existing BF16 pow2 uses the old col-major ABI.
implementation.failure: The new native quantizer uses the original sequence device status. A real status-reset prefix is retained across later launch errors; NaN/+Inf fails the original Completion and publishes no successful Graph result. No CPU readback/executor is introduced.
implementation.ownership: Existing immutable provider plan, invocation workspace, original runtime retirement and Graph caller/result leases. Native kernel loading finishes during prepare, before replay/capture.

validation.inputs: Nonunit/nonpower2 group maxima, non-BF16-representable F32 values adjacent to E4 RNE boundaries, distinct row/group scales, nonpower2 original F32 weight scales and partial N tiles.
validation.oracle: Independent scalar code table, RNE enumeration, frexp power2 scale and explicit F32 boundaries; sparse code-domain dots isolate layout/operand/output arithmetic without a vendor reduction-tree claim.
validation.paired_graph: CPU executes2steps; CUDA executes1selected shared-prologue pair step, so the two-output shared native quantization path actually runs.
validation.lifetime: Old readonly results remain exact across independent NaN/+Inf failures, later successful generation and compiled-plan release.

fixture_correction.cause: Focused test used owned bindings before calling Invocation::prepare_resources; both backends rejected before any new dynamic linear submission. Added normal prepare_resources; no product graph/provider/math/guard relaxation.

validation.fixture_limit: The initial focused test forgot Invocation::prepare_resources before owned bindings; both backends rejected before executing the new dynamic linear. The normal binding API fixed this test error; no product resource guard was relaxed.

source_binding.statement: This closes a genuine generic CUDA combination gap. It does not assert that the two pinned Qwen FP8 sources require F32 activation or this PowerOfTwo reader policy; source configs only establish dynamic block128 FP8 and Q24 bfloat16.
source_binding.historical_note: The older frozen source-tile proof correctly records that F32 dynamic PowerOfTwo was then unavailable; its F32 profile explicitly used already encoded A MatMul. That archive was not rewritten.

tooling.scope: Only the provider TU and existing quantize-output test TU were incrementally compiled, reusing native kernels, cubins and existing CPU/CUDA SDK closure.

limitations: No model weights were acquired or new complete model executed for this generic function fix.
No throughput, physical-memory peak or BF16 performance comparison was run.
CUDA still uses the existing SM89 AOT GEMM qualification; no claim is made for another GPU architecture.
Commands replay was measured for correctness. No new capture-specific claim is signed by these two tests.
No SDK, object, executable, cubin body or model tensor is embedded in this archive.
